/-!
This finite-place arithmetic API is ported from `iut`'s Corollary 3.12
`ThetaData/Places` layer and its concrete `Concrete/LocalTheory` layer.  It is
a local definition over the mathlib finite-place carrier; no `iut` module is
imported as a dependency.
-/

/-- The ramification index of a finite place over its residue characteristic. -/
noncomputable def ramIdx (w : NumberField.FinitePlace K) : ℕ :=
  Ideal.ramificationIdx w.maximalIdeal.asIdeal ℤ

/-- The residue degree of a finite place over its residue characteristic. -/
noncomputable def inertDeg (w : NumberField.FinitePlace K) : ℕ :=
  Ideal.inertiaDeg w.maximalIdeal.asIdeal ℤ

import ArithmeticTeichmullerSpaces.Prologue.Arithmetic.Basic

namespace JoshiTeich.Prologue.Theta

/-!
The Tate-parameter boundary records the local parameter function separately
from the theta-link laws.  The source describes a Tate parameter as a
nonzero element with nontrivial finite-place absolute value; the strict
`norm_lt_one` condition is the local Tate-uniformization condition.
-/

structure TateParameterData (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] where
  places : Finset (NumberField.FinitePlace K)
  /-- The Tate parameter at `w`, as an element of the local completion `K_w`. -/
  parameter : (w : NumberField.FinitePlace K) → w.maximalIdeal.adicCompletion K
  norm : NumberField.FinitePlace K → ℝ

structure TateParameterLaws {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    (T : TateParameterData K) : Prop where
  places_nonempty : T.places.Nonempty
  parameter_nonzero : ∀ w ∈ T.places, T.parameter w ≠ 0
  norm_eq : ∀ w ∈ T.places, T.norm w = ‖T.parameter w‖
  norm_pos : ∀ w ∈ T.places, 0 < T.norm w
  norm_lt_one : ∀ w ∈ T.places, T.norm w < 1

/-!
# The Tate `q`-parameter

This file introduces the *Tate parameter* attached to a Tate elliptic curve: an element
`q` of the base field with `0 < ‖q‖ < 1`, together with its normalized additive order.

Over a complete nonarchimedean field `K`, a Tate curve is uniformized by the analytic

because `0 < ‖q‖ < 1`. This module isolates the purely metric core of that datum, which
needs neither the nonarchimedean (ultrametric) hypothesis nor completeness: those enter in
the later files that build the `qᶻ`-action, the analytic quotient and the uniformization.

/-!
# The discrete normalized order of the Tate parameter

When the norm of `K` is *discrete* — its value group on `Kˣ` is generated by the norm of a
**uniformizer** `π` (`IsUniformizer`) — the real-valued order `ord q = -log ‖q‖` of a Tate
parameter refines to a canonical positive integer: the unique `n` with `‖q‖ = ‖π‖ⁿ`. This
is the **normalized additive order** of the `q`-parameter in the convention of IUT I,
Definition 3.1(c): the additive valuation is normalized so that `ord π = 1`, and then
`ord q = orderZ ∈ ℤ_{>0}` (`ord_eq_orderZ_mul`). It supplies the canonical value for the
`orderNat` seam of `OrderedTateParameter` (`toOrdered`), on which the Θ-data coprimality
predicate `PrimeToOrder` operates.

**Local vs. global.** The datum formalized here is the *local* `q`-parameter of a Tate
curve over one complete nonarchimedean field, and its normalized local order/height. The
*global* `q`-pilot object of IUT (a collection of local `q`-parameters at the bad places,
entering the log-volume computations) is a different, later construction layered on top
of these local data; only the local convention is fixed in this repository.

import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Basic
import TateCurvesTheta.QParameter.Basic

/-!
# Coprimality to the order of the Tate `q`-parameter

Initial Θ-data (Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory I*, Definition 3.1(c))
requires a prime `ℓ` that is *prime to the order of the `q`-parameter*: the multiplicative
order datum attached to the Tate curve must be coprime to `ℓ`. This file isolates that
purely arithmetic condition.

The **order** meant here is the *discrete normalized additive valuation* of `q`, a positive
natural number: over a complete nonarchimedean field it equals the number of irreducible
components of the special fibre of the Tate curve `E_q`. The real-valued order
`TateParameter.ord` of `TateCurvesTheta.QParameter.Basic` refines to this integer once a
normalized additive valuation is fixed; that normalization is supplied by the shared
valuation infrastructure and is not yet available in this repository. Until then the
discrete order is carried as data on `OrderedTateParameter`, which is the seam where the
canonical value will later be plugged in.

import TateCurvesTheta.TateCurve.Discriminant

/-!
# The `j`-invariant of the Tate curve

The `j`-invariant of `E_q : y² + xy = x³ + a₄x + a₆` as an explicit element of `K`:
`tateJ = c₄³/Δ` with `c₄ = 1 - 48a₄`. Ultrametrically the invariants have exact norms
`‖c₄‖ = 1` and `‖Δ‖ = ‖q‖` (`Discriminant.lean`), so

* `norm_tateJ` : `‖j(E_q)‖ = ‖q‖⁻¹`, in particular
* `one_lt_norm_tateJ` : `‖j(E_q)‖ > 1` — the Tate curve always has non-integral
  `j`-invariant, the analytic incarnation of potentially multiplicative reduction.

This is the input for the existence and uniqueness of the Tate parameter with prescribed
`j`-invariant (`QParameter/JParametrization.lean`): `q ↦ j(E_q)` is an injective map onto
`{j : ‖j‖ > 1}`.

## Main definitions and results

* `TateCurvesTheta.TateParameter.tateJ`: the `j`-invariant `c₄³/Δ` of `E_q`.
